en.title: Count Integers with an Odd Number of Zero Digits
en.description:
Using standard decimal representation, count the elements in which the digit 0 appears an odd number of times; the integer 0 itself is written as a single 0 and qualifies.

This site's standard input/output is stated explicitly; ranges not given by the source problem are marked as this site's conventions.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n integers; 1≤n≤1000, 0≤a[i]≤10⁹.
en.explanation: Example 1: 20, 10, and 10070 contain 1, 1, and 3 zeros respectively, so the answer is 3. Example 2: 0 contains one 0 and qualifies, while 100 contains two and does not, so the answer is 1. Example 3: 1010 has two 0s and does not qualify, while 10100 has three 0s and qualifies, so the answer is 1.
hints: Convert each number to a standard decimal string, count its 0s, and check the parity.
